hint.text: Conjunctions are joining words. They can join together two words, phrases or sentences.

atoms.b: Paul cooked ((and)) I did the dishes.
atoms.sound: Paul cooked and I did the dishes.

hint.text: Conjunctions are joining words. They can join together two words, phrases or sentences.

atoms.b: Do you want ice cream ((or)) cake for dessert?
atoms.sound: Do you want ice cream or cake for dessert?

hint.text: Conjunctions are joining words. They can join together two words, phrases or sentences.

atoms.b: I can’t come to your party ((because)) I’m not feeling well.
atoms.sound: I can’t come to your party because I’m not feeling well.

hint.text: Conjunctions are joining words. They can join together two words, phrases or sentences.

atoms.b: Kareem was hungry, ((so)) he ate a sandwich.
atoms.sound: Kareem was hungry, so he ate a sandwich.

hint.text: Conjunctions are joining words. They can join together two words, phrases or sentences.

atoms.b: I would watch a film with you, ((but)) I’m too tired.
atoms.sound: I would watch a film with you, but I’m too tired.

hint.text: Conjunctions are joining words. They can join together two words, phrases or sentences.

atoms.b: We can go to the cinema ((after)) we finish cleaning the kitchen.
atoms.sound: We can go to the cinema after we finish cleaning the kitchen.

hint.text: Conjunctions are joining words. They can join together two words, phrases or sentences.

atoms.b: I want to finish my homework ((before)) having dinner.
atoms.sound: I want to finish my homework before having dinner.

hint.text: Conjunctions are joining words. They can join together two words, phrases or sentences.

atoms.b: We went outside ((although)) it was raining.
atoms.sound: We went outside although it was raining.

hint.text: Conjunctions are joining words. They can join together two words, phrases or sentences.

atoms.b: We would be thrilled ((if)) we won the competition.
atoms.sound: We would be thrilled if we won the competition.
